div.head: Hn com 3.1
div.ab: Et si est inter uauasores alicuius baronis mei honoris, tractetur placitum in curia domini eorum.
Et si est inter vavasores alicuius baronis mei honoris, tractetur placitum in curia domini eorum.
And if it is between the vassals of a crown baron of mine, the case shall be dealt with in their lord's court.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 286–287 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 524, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: Sind beide Parteien Aftervassallen eines Kronbarons, so unterstehen sie dessen Lehnsgericht. Den Satz benutzt Hn 25, 1. Vgl. Constit. Clarendon. 9: Si uterque der Parteien, clericus et laicus advocaverit de feudo illo ante eundem baronem, erit placitum in curia ipsius, sonst in curia regia

If both parties are under-vassals of one baron of the Crown, they are subject to his feudal court. The sentence is used by Hn 25, 1. Cf. Constit. Clarendon. 9: Si uterque of the parties, clericus et laicus advocaverit de feudo illo ante eundem baronem, erit placitum in curia ipsius, otherwise in curia regia
